MCP surface modernization: adopt 2025-2026 best practices (tracker)

# MCP surface modernization: adopt 2025-2026 best practices

Tracking issue. Driven by an audit of archy's MCP surface against a verified deep-research pass on current MCP best practices (Anthropic engineering guidance + the modelcontextprotocol.io spec, 2025-2026).

## Verdict: yes, the surface is getting messy

archy exposes **19 MCP tools** (~2.5-3k tokens of descriptions always in context) on the official `mcp` SDK FastMCP (`mcp>=1.27.1`, which already supports `annotations` / `title` / `structured_output`). The concrete gaps:

| Sub-issue | Gap | Effort / value |
|---|---|---|
| #225 | **Zero tool annotations** -- all 19 are read-only but none declares `readOnlyHint`, so clients cannot auto-approve and assume destructive/open-world defaults | low / high |
| #226 | **Token-heavy responses, no compact-by-default** -- `archy_dsm` ~57KB, `archy_graph` up to 500 nodes; no cap / detail mode | med-high / high |
| #228 | **structuredContent + outputSchema** (2025-06-18) not verified/explicit | low-med / med |
| #229 | **Inconsistent error model** -- union `*ErrorPayload` vs raises; no single recovery contract | med / med |
| #227 | **Tool sprawl + redundancy** -- graph x4, refactor x3 (one fuses two), impact x2, score/baseline overlap; consolidate 19 -> ~12-13 (BC-breaking epic) | high / high |

## Key research findings (all high-confidence, adversarially verified)
- Tool definitions consume context before any work; 58 tools ~= 55K tokens (Anthropic has seen 134K), and **large counts degrade selection accuracy**, worst with similar names. [anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use; code-execution-with-mcp]
- **More tools != better**; build a few thoughtful, workflow-matched, namespaced tools. [writing-tools-for-agents]
- On-demand discovery (Tool Search Tool `defer_loading`) pays off at **10+ tools or >10K tokens of defs** (~85% token cut, accuracy gains in Anthropic evals). It is *client* configuration; the **server-side lever is a lean, tight surface** (#227) + small definitions.
- Cap and shape responses: Claude Code defaults to **25K tokens**; paginate / filter / truncate; concise-by-default with a `response_format` enum; high-signal data with human-meaningful ids. [writing-tools-for-agents]
- **Annotate read-only tools** (`readOnlyHint:true`, `openWorldHint:false`, `destructiveHint:false`); clients may auto-approve them. [mcp tool-annotations blog]
- Two error mechanisms: JSON-RPC protocol errors vs `isError:true` tool results. [2025-06-18 server spec]

## Spec-revision timeline (what an existing server adopts)
- **2025-03-26:** tool annotations (`readOnlyHint` etc.) -> #225.
- **2025-06-18:** structured output (`structuredContent`/`outputSchema`), the `title` field, OAuth authorization, elicitation, a security-best-practices page -> #228, #225 (title).

## Sequencing
1. **Low-risk wins first:** #225 (annotations + title), #228 (structured output verify), #226 (response shaping). None removes a tool, so no plugin-pin/tool-count churn.
2. #229 (error-model standardization) -- coordinate the error shape with #228.
3. #227 (consolidation) is the BC-breaking epic: removing/renaming tools needs a plugin-pin lower-bound bump + tool-count updates everywhere + a deliberate version boundary. Sequence last.

## Open questions (not yet ticketed)
- **Resources primitive:** archy uses tools + prompts but not MCP Resources. Evaluate whether large read-only reference artifacts (full graph, DSM) fit Resources better than tools. Lower priority; revisit during #226/#227.
- **Code-execution / Programmatic Tool Calling** (200KB -> 1KB in Anthropic's example): largely a client capability, but #226's summary-first shaping is the server-side enabler.

## Gap / question
archy returns Pydantic models that FastMCP serializes to JSON. The **2025-06-18** spec added structured tool output (`structuredContent` + an optional `outputSchema` on the Tool). It is unclear what archy currently emits on the wire and whether it is taking full advantage.

## Best practice (sourced)
- 2025-06-18 added `structuredContent` (JSON object) plus optional `outputSchema` (JSON Schema); servers that declare `outputSchema` MUST return conforming results and clients SHOULD validate -- enabling strict validation, type info, better parsing. [modelcontextprotocol.io 2025-06-18 changelog/server/schema]
- For backwards compatibility a tool returning `structuredContent` SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a `TextContent` block; clients SHOULD prefer **`content` for conversational/agent UX (lower tokens)**. [2025-06-18 server spec; PR #559]

## Concrete fix
- The SDK supports it: `FastMCP.tool` accepts `structured_output`. Confirm (via a live `tools/list` + a `tools/call`) what archy actually emits today for its Pydantic returns -- does it already attach `outputSchema` and `structuredContent`?
- If not automatic, opt in so each tool declares an `outputSchema` derived from its return model, and ensure a text `content` block is also returned for token-efficient agent UX.
- Document the wire shape in `docs/` so it is a known property.

## Effort / impact
Low-medium (mostly verification + explicit opt-in + docs). Likely partially free via FastMCP; the value is making it explicit and correct. Part of the MCP-modernization sweep.

# Spec: `archy_graph` MCP tool

Open roadmap item from README:

> `archy graph` MCP tool: expose the dep graph itself for agent-side reasoning

The CLI command `archy graph` already exists and emits `text` / `json` / `dot`. The work is wiring it into `src/archy/mcp.py` next to the other nine tools - but a naïve "dump the full graph JSON" tool wastes the agent's context on every call. This spec defines a small set of lenses tuned for how agents actually reason about a graph.

## Why not one big dump

A full graph for a medium project (a few hundred modules, a few thousand edges) easily blows past 100k tokens once you include node attrs (`path`, `is_package`, `external`, `instability`) and edge attrs (`lines`, `is_relative`). Agents rarely need all of it - they need:

- "what does this module depend on / who depends on it"  (the local neighborhood - the by-far most common query)
- "what's the shape of the whole project"  (a summary view, not 3000 edges)
- "give me everything so I can do my own analysis"  (rare, but the CLI already serves this)

The other dep-graph MCP servers we surveyed converge on the same split:

- **sentrux** ships a `dsm` (Dependency Structure Matrix) tool - a compact whole-graph summary, distinct from the raw-graph endpoint
- **mkearl/dependency-mcp** has `get_dependency_graph` (full) *and* `get_file_metadata` (single-file focus)
- **entrepeneur4lyf/code-graph-mcp** exposes `find_callers` / `find_callees` - neighborhood queries, not full dumps
- **oraios/serena** is the strongest signal here: "agent-first tool design… robust high-level abstractions… distinguishing it from approaches that rely on low-level concepts"

Takeaway: a `graph` namespace with three tools, not one.

## Proposed tools

### 1. `archy_graph_focus(path, modules, depth=1, direction="both")`

The primary tool. Returns a slice of the graph centered on one or more modules.

**Parameters**
- `modules: list[str]` - qualnames (e.g. `["archy.parser"]`) **or** file paths that resolve to internal modules (uses the shared `resolve_modules` helper, same path resolution as `find_impact`). Multi-seed: ego graphs are unioned across all resolved seeds; unresolved entries are returned in the `unresolved` field instead of erroring.
- `depth: int = 1` - how many hops to expand
- `direction: "in" | "out" | "both" = "both"` - `in` = who depends on me (callers), `out` = my dependencies, `both` = bidirectional neighborhood
- `internal_only: bool = True`

**Returns** - same `_graph_to_dict` shape the CLI emits, but only the subgraph reachable within `depth` hops in the requested direction(s). Each node carries `instability`; each edge carries `lines` so the agent can pinpoint the import site.

**Why this shape**: `find_impact` already gives reverse-reachability of *internal* modules; this generalizes it (forward direction, depth-limited, with edge detail). Agents use this before editing - same role as `archy_impact` but more flexible.

238	## MCP server (`archy mcp`)
239	
240	The server is backed by a persistent parse cache (`.archy/index.db`): each tool call re-parses only the files whose content changed since the last call, so warm graph builds stay in the low seconds even on very large repos (benchmarked: 21.5s cold to 2.5s warm on Home Assistant's 17,299 modules). The cache is transparent and disposable; deleting `.archy/index.db` only costs one cold rebuild. The graph is always re-derived from the current files, so a cached result is never stale. `archy index sync` warms it explicitly; `archy index clear` removes it.
241	
242	`archy mcp` exposes nineteen tools and one prompt to MCP-aware AI agents (Claude Code, the Anthropic API, etc.):
243	
244	| Tool | Purpose |
245	|---|---|
246	| `archy_score` | Compute the five-metric score (modularity, acyclicity, depth, equality, complexity, geometric mean); optional `record=True` and `strict=True` for the same regression-gate behaviour the CLI offers. |
247	| `archy_cycles` | Find import cycles. |

## MCP server (`archy mcp`)

The server is backed by a persistent parse cache (`.archy/index.db`): each tool call re-parses only the files whose content changed since the last call, so warm graph builds stay in the low seconds even on very large repos (benchmarked: 21.5s cold to 2.5s warm on Home Assistant's 17,299 modules). The cache is transparent and disposable; deleting `.archy/index.db` only costs one cold rebuild. The graph is always re-derived from the current files, so a cached result is never stale. `archy index sync` warms it explicitly; `archy index clear` removes it.

`archy mcp` exposes nineteen tools and one prompt to MCP-aware AI agents (Claude Code, the Anthropic API, etc.):

| `archy_score` | Compute the five-metric score (modularity, acyclicity, depth, equality, complexity, geometric mean); optional `record=True` and `strict=True` for the same regression-gate behaviour the CLI offers. |

Tool returns are pydantic models; FastMCP serializes them to JSON for
the MCP client. The model shapes are the public wire contract for any
agent calling these tools.

## Structured output (2025-06-18 spec)

FastMCP derives an `outputSchema` (JSON Schema) from each tool's return
annotation and attaches it to the `tools/list` entry, so every archy tool
declares its result shape up front. Each `tools/call` then returns BOTH a
machine-readable `structuredContent` (the JSON object, validated against
that schema) AND a `TextContent` block carrying the same JSON serialized,
which clients may prefer for token-efficient agent UX. archy gets this for
free from the SDK; no per-tool opt-in is needed.

Two wrapping rules worth knowing:

- A tool whose return is a bare sequence (`list[Cycle]` for `archy_cycles`,
  `list[TrendRow]` for `archy_trend`) is wrapped under a top-level `result`
  key, because `structuredContent` MUST be a JSON object, not an array.
- A tool whose return is a union (`DiffReport | DiffErrorPayload`,
  `GraphPayload | GraphTooLargePayload`, `DSM | DSMDiff | DSMErrorPayload`)
  is likewise wrapped under `result`, with the union expressed as the
  schema's `anyOf`; every branch (including the `*ErrorPayload` ones) is a
  conforming member, so an in-band error result still validates.

One benign edge: an *empty* sequence return yields `structuredContent`
`{"result": []}` with no accompanying `TextContent` block (FastMCP emits one
content block per element). The structured form is unambiguous, so this is
not a correctness gap. tests/test_mcp.py locks the whole contract.
"""

Tool returns are pydantic models; FastMCP serializes them to JSON for
the MCP client. The model shapes are the public wire contract for any
agent calling these tools.

## Structured output (2025-06-18 spec)

FastMCP derives an `outputSchema` (JSON Schema) from each tool's return
annotation and attaches it to the `tools/list` entry, so every archy tool
declares its result shape up front. Each `tools/call` then returns BOTH a
machine-readable `structuredContent` (the JSON object, validated against
that schema) AND a `TextContent` block carrying the same JSON serialized,
which clients may prefer for token-efficient agent UX. archy gets this for
free from the SDK; no per-tool opt-in is needed.

Two wrapping rules worth knowing:

- A tool whose return is a bare sequence (`list[Cycle]` for `archy_cycles`,
  `list[TrendRow]` for `archy_trend`) is wrapped under a top-level `result`
  key, because `structuredContent` MUST be a JSON object, not an array.
- A tool whose return is a union (`DiffReport | DiffErrorPayload`,
  `GraphPayload | GraphTooLargePayload`, `DSM | DSMDiff | DSMErrorPayload`)
  is likewise wrapped under `result`, with the union expressed as the
  schema's `anyOf`; every branch (including the `*ErrorPayload` ones) is a
  conforming member, so an in-band error result still validates.

One benign edge: an *empty* sequence return yields `structuredContent`
`{"result": []}` with no accompanying `TextContent` block (FastMCP emits one
content block per element). The structured form is unambiguous, so this is
not a correctness gap. tests/test_mcp.py locks the whole contract.
"""

def test_all_tools_declare_output_schema():
    # 2025-06-18 structured output: FastMCP derives an `outputSchema` (JSON
    # Schema) from each tool's return annotation. Assert every tool declares
    # one and it is an object schema, since `structuredContent` must be a JSON
    # object (sequence/union returns are wrapped under a `result` key to honor
    # this -- see the module docstring).
    server = create_server()
    tools = asyncio.run(server.list_tools())
    for tool in tools:

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    # One case per wrapping rule the structured-output contract has to honor.
    # expect_text is the BC guidance that a `TextContent` block accompanies
    # `structuredContent`; it is False only for an empty bare-sequence return,
    # which FastMCP serializes to zero content blocks (the documented benign
    # edge in the module docstring).
    ("name", "extra_args", "expect_text"),
    [
        ("archy_score", {}, True),  # BaseModel return
        ("archy_graph", {}, True),  # union, success branch (GraphPayload)
        ("archy_diff", {}, True),  # union, in-band error branch (no baseline -> DiffErrorPayload)
        ("archy_cycles", {}, False),  # bare list, empty on an acyclic project -> {"result": []}
    ],
)
def test_tool_result_conforms_to_output_schema(
    acyclic_project: Path, name: str, extra_args: dict, expect_text: bool
):
    # A client that validates `structuredContent` against a declared
    # `outputSchema` MUST NOT reject archy's results -- including the in-band
    # `*ErrorPayload` branch of a union return, which is an `anyOf` member of
    # the schema, not a separate error channel.
    from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator

    server = create_server()
    schema = {t.name: t.outputSchema for t in asyncio.run(server.list_tools())}[name]
    content, structured = asyncio.run(
        server.call_tool(name, {"path": str(acyclic_project), **extra_args})
    )
    assert isinstance(structured, dict)
    errors = sorted(
        Draft202012Validator(schema).iter_errors(structured), key=lambda e: list(e.path)
    )
    assert not errors, f"{name} structuredContent violates outputSchema: {errors[:1]}"
    has_text = any(getattr(block, "text", None) for block in content)
    assert has_text is expect_text

import asyncio, tempfile
from pathlib import Path

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())

async def main():
    params = StdioServerParameters(command="archy", args=["mcp"])
    async with stdio_client(params) as (r, w):
        async with ClientSession(r, w) as s:
            await s.initialize()
            tools = (await s.list_tools()).tools
            print(f"tools/list -> {len(tools)} tools")
            t = next(x for x in tools if x.name == "archy_score")
            print("archy_score title:", t.title)
            print("archy_score annotations:", t.annotations.model_dump(exclude_none=True) if t.annotations else None)
            print("archy_score has outputSchema:", bool(t.outputSchema))
            n_ann = sum(1 for x in tools if x.annotations and x.annotations.readOnlyHint)
            n_os = sum(1 for x in tools if x.outputSchema)
            print(f"readOnlyHint set: {n_ann}/{len(tools)} | outputSchema set: {n_os}/{len(tools)}")
            res = await s.call_tool("archy_score", {"path": str(d)})
            print("\ntools/call archy_score:")
            print("  content blocks:", [type(c).__name__ for c in res.content])
            print("  structuredContent keys:", list((res.structuredContent or {}).keys()))

#233 merged and #228 closed. Now, your question:

## Yes — #226 needs doc updates, and more than the last two did

Unlike #225/#228 (which were metadata/contract-only), **#226 actually changes tool behavior** — concise-by-default responses, a truncation cap, and a `detail`/`response_format` param on the token-heavy tools. That ripples into several doc surfaces:

1. **In-code `description=` strings in `mcp.py`** — these are the *most important* docs because they're the wire-level text the agent reads to decide how to call a tool. The new `detail`/`response_format` param and the "concise by default, ask for full" behavior must be described there, especially for `archy_dsm` (~57KB today) and `archy_graph` (up to 500 nodes). If we don't, agents won't know the knob exists.

2. **README MCP tool table** (lines 259/263) — the `archy_dsm` and `archy_graph` rows need the new param + the truncation-cap note.

3. **`docs/SPEC_GRAPH_MCP.md`** — this spec explicitly argues "why not one big dump" and defines the graph lenses; a truncation cap + detail mode is squarely in scope and should be folded in so the spec stays the source of truth.

4. **`docs/AGENT_LOOP.md`** — only if the cap changes the recommended cadence (e.g. "start with summary, request detail when needed"). Probably a light touch.

The DeepWork **doc-sync rule will flag any drift** I miss between `mcp.py` and the README/docs, same as it did on the last PRs — so it's self-enforcing, but I'd rather write the docs deliberately than patch them after a review flag.

One thing worth settling *before* I start #226, since it shapes both code and docs: **the response-shaping API surface**. The ticket floats two framings — a boolean-ish `detail` flag vs. a `response_format` enum (e.g. `concise`/`full`). Want me to decide that as part of the implementation plan, or do you have a preference? I'll otherwise pick the enum (more extensible, matches the spec's `response_format` language) and surface it in the plan for your sign-off.

Want me to start #226 now (I'll plan first, then implement + docs + tests in one PR)?

content.content:
MCP: concise-by-default responses + truncation cap + detail mode on token-heavy tools (dsm, graph)

## Gap
Several archy tools return large payloads straight into the agent context with no compact-by-default mode or cap:
- `archy_dsm` can return ~57KB of JSON (flagged previously as the bounded-output / cognitive-overload antipattern).
- `archy_graph` returns up to `max_nodes=500` nodes.
- `archy_graph_summary` exists as a SEPARATE tool rather than a detail mode of `archy_graph`.

## Best practice (sourced)
- Returning large raw outputs into context is harmful; Anthropic's Programmatic Tool Calling / code-execution-with-MCP pattern cut one payload from **200KB to ~1KB** and reduced average token use 43,588 -> 27,297 (-37%) with accuracy gains. [anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use; code-execution-with-mcp]
- Tool responses should be **capped and shaped**: Claude Code restricts tool responses to **25,000 tokens by default** and recommends pagination / range selection / filtering / truncation with sensible defaults. Oversized un-paginated responses cause real context-limit failures. [anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents]
- Return only **high-signal** data with human-meaningful identifiers; a **`response_format` enum lets the agent choose concise vs detailed** output. [writing-tools-for-agents]

## Concrete fix

class DSMCell(BaseModel):
    """A non-empty entry in the matrix. (row, col) index into `DSM.ordering`."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    row: int
    col: int
    weight: float


class DSMGroup(BaseModel):
    """A contiguous block of `ordering` sharing a group label."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    label: str
    members: tuple[str, ...]


class DSM(BaseModel):
    """Sparse DSM. `ordering` is the row/col order; `cells` lists non-empty entries.

    `groups[i].members` is a contiguous slice of `ordering`. Cell positions
    are int indices into `ordering`, so an agent can reconstruct the dense
    matrix by walking cells and indexing by `(row, col)`.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    ordering: tuple[str, ...]
    groups: tuple[DSMGroup, ...]
    cells: tuple[DSMCell, ...]
    group_by: GroupBy
    weight: Weight


class DSMDiff(BaseModel):
    """Structured diff between two DSMs over the union of their nodes.

    Edges are matched by (source_name, target_name), so node additions and
    removals are tracked explicitly in `nodes_added` / `nodes_removed`. Cell
    indices are ordering-relative: `added` / `new_back_edges` index `after`,
    while `removed` index `before`; never index one's cells into the other.

    `new_back_edges` is the load-bearing field for agent scenario 2 in
    `docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md`: cells that appeared above the diagonal in
    `after` but did not exist in `before`, meaning the edit introduced a
    new back-edge in the chosen ordering.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    added: tuple[DSMCell, ...]
    removed: tuple[DSMCell, ...]
    weight_changed: tuple[tuple[DSMCell, DSMCell], ...]
    nodes_added: tuple[str, ...]
    nodes_removed: tuple[str, ...]
    new_back_edges: tuple[DSMCell, ...]


def build_dsm(
    graph: nx.DiGraph,
    *,
    group_by: GroupBy = "community",
    weight: Weight = "imports",
    focus: str | None = None,
    focus_depth: int = 1,
    package: str | None = None,
) -> DSM:
    """Build a DSM from an import graph.

    Operates on the internal subgraph (external nodes excluded; the
    audience is structural reasoning about your own code, not vendor
    surface). Applies `focus` and `package` filters in that order.
    """
    sub = _internal_subgraph(graph)
    if package is not None:
        sub = _filter_by_package(sub, package)
    if focus is not None:
        sub = _filter_by_focus(sub, focus, focus_depth)

    if group_by == "community":
        groups = _group_by_community(sub)
    elif group_by == "layer":
        groups = _group_by_layer(sub)
    else:
        groups = _group_by_topological(sub)

# Plan: #226 — concise-by-default responses on `archy_dsm` / `archy_graph`

## Context

archy exposes 19 read-only MCP tools. A few return large payloads straight into the agent's
context with no compact-by-default mode and no cap:
- `archy_dsm` returns the full sparse matrix (every cell + every module name in `ordering`/`groups`);
  ~13KB on archy itself, ~57KB on larger repos (flagged earlier as the bounded-output antipattern).
- `archy_graph` dumps up to `max_nodes=500` nodes with all node/edge attrs (~42KB measured).

Best practice (Anthropic *writing-tools-for-agents*; the 2025-06-18 sweep, tracker #230) is
**concise-by-default with a `response_format` enum** so the agent opts into the heavy payload, plus
a cap with explicit truncation indicators. This is the first behavior-changing ticket of the sweep
(#225 annotations and #228 structured-output were metadata/contract only) and has the highest
agent-edit-loop impact.

**Decision taken (user):** default `response_format="summary"` for **both** tools. No-arg calls
return concise output; `response_format="full"` returns the heavy payload (capped).

## Design

### New param (both tools)
Add `response_format: str = "summary"` to `archy_dsm` and `archy_graph`. Validate
`in {"summary", "full"}`, else raise `ValueError(f"response_format must be 'summary' or 'full'; got {response_format!r}")`
— matches the existing validation convention in `mcp.py` (e.g. `_run_graph_focus` direction check).

### `archy_graph`
- `summary` (default): delegate to the existing `_run_graph_summary` path (returns the proven
  `GraphSummaryPayload`: top-N fan-in/out/PageRank/edit-risk + external deps). Reuse `top_n` (default 20).
- `full`: existing `_run_graph_dump` (→ `GraphPayload | GraphTooLargePayload`, `max_nodes` guard unchanged).
- Return union becomes `GraphSummaryPayload | GraphPayload | GraphTooLargePayload`.
- Keep the separate `archy_graph_summary` tool for now (removing it is tool-removal = the #227
  consolidation epic). Note the equivalence in both tools' descriptions.

### `archy_dsm`
- New compact model `DSMSummary` in `src/archy/dsm.py` (frozen `BaseModel`), bounded independent of
  module count (the full DSM's size is dominated by `ordering`/`groups.members` + `cells`):
  - `group_by`, `weight` (echo)
  - `module_count` (= len ordering), `cell_count` (= len cells), `group_count`
  - `groups: tuple[DSMGroupSummary, ...]` where `DSMGroupSummary = {label, size}` — block structure
    WITHOUT the member name lists
  - `back_edge_count` + `top_back_edges: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]` (a few source→target names that
    sit above the diagonal in the ordering = the cycle-localizing signal; cap ~10). Reuse the
    back-edge convention already used by `diff_dsm`'s `new_back_edges` (cell with `row < col` after
    topological/SCC ordering).
  - `cross_group_edge_count` (edges whose endpoints fall in different groups = coupling)
  - Add a `summarize_dsm(dsm: DSM) -> DSMSummary` pure helper in `dsm.py` (derives all fields from an
    already-built `DSM`, so `build_dsm` stays unchanged and the CLI is unaffected).
- `summary` (default): `summarize_dsm(build_dsm(...))`.
- `full`: existing `build_dsm(...)` → `DSM`, but capped (see below).
- Diff path (`baseline_path` set) is unchanged — `DSMDiff` is already compact (`new_back_edges` is the
  signal) and is a deliberate diff, not a dump. `response_format` does not apply to the diff path
  (document this).
- Return union becomes `DSMSummary | DSM | DSMDiff | DSMTooLargePayload | DSMErrorPayload`.

### Truncation cap (full mode only)
Mirror the existing `GraphTooLargePayload` union-refusal pattern (consistent, deterministic, no
token-counting). For `archy_dsm(response_format="full")`, if `len(cells) > max_cells` (new
`DEFAULT_MAX_DSM_CELLS`, ~2000), return a new `DSMTooLargePayload`
`{error, cell_count, max_cells}` whose message points to `response_format="summary"` /
`focus=` / `package=` as the escape hatches (same shape/wording style as `GraphTooLargePayload`).
`archy_graph` full mode keeps its existing `max_nodes`→`GraphTooLargePayload` guard.

### Out of scope (deliberate)
- CLI (`archy dsm`, `archy graph`) stays unchanged — confirmed independent of the MCP code paths;
  renders to a human-driven terminal; this ticket is MCP-scoped.
- Removing/folding `archy_graph_summary` → #227 (BC-breaking, sequenced last).
- Tool count stays 19 → no plugin-pin bump, no manifest/registry count edits.

## Files to change

### Code
- `src/archy/dsm.py` — add `DSMGroupSummary`, `DSMSummary` models + `summarize_dsm()` helper.
- `src/archy/mcp.py` —
  - import `DSMSummary` (+ `summarize_dsm`); add `DSMTooLargePayload` model + `DEFAULT_MAX_DSM_CELLS`.
  - `archy_dsm`: new `response_format` param, branch summary/full, cap full mode, widen return union +
    rewrite `description=`.
  - `archy_graph`: new `response_format` param, branch summary(→`_run_graph_summary`)/full, widen
    return union + rewrite `description=`; surface `top_n`.
  - `archy_graph_summary` description: cross-reference `archy_graph(response_format="summary")`.
  - `_AGENT_LOOP_PROMPT`: update the `archy_dsm` / graph guidance to reflect summary-by-default.

### Docs (thorough — the user's explicit ask; the doc-sync `.deepreview` rule also enforces drift)
- `README.md` — MCP tool table rows for `archy_dsm`, `archy_graph`, `archy_graph_summary`
  (~lines 257–263): document `response_format`, the summary default, and the cap. Touch the
  "Tool output contract" note (~line 270) only if needed.
- `docs/SPEC_GRAPH_MCP.md` — the design source of truth for the three graph tools: add
  `response_format` + summary-default + cap to the `archy_graph` section (and note the
  graph_summary relationship / #227 fold).
- `docs/AGENT_LOOP.md` — update the `archy_graph` / `archy_dsm` call examples for summary-by-default.
- `plugins/claude/skills/archy/SKILL.md` — update any dsm/graph call examples to match (it mirrors
  the agent-loop guidance).
- `docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md` — verify the "visualization-only" framing / any payload-size note
  still reads correctly with summary-as-default; light touch if so.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` — add a shipped/changelog line if that's where features are logged (verify
  convention at implementation time).
- LEAVE as accurate dated records (repo convention): `docs/FUTURE.md`, `docs/LEARNINGS.md` historical
  entries — do not rewrite; add a new dated entry only if the file's pattern calls for one.
- NO change: plugin.json, marketplace.json, MCP_DIRECTORIES.md (count stays 19); cli.py.

### Tests (`tests/test_mcp.py`, `tests/test_dsm.py`)
- `response_format` validation: bad value raises on both tools.
- `archy_dsm` summary returns `DSMSummary` (no `cells`/member lists; counts present); full returns
  `DSM` with cells; full oversized → `DSMTooLargePayload`.
- `archy_graph` summary returns `GraphSummaryPayload`; full returns `GraphPayload` as before.
- default (no `response_format`) is summary for both.
- `summarize_dsm()` unit test in `test_dsm.py` (counts, back-edge localization, cross-group count) on
  a known small graph incl. a cycle.
- Extend the structured-output conformance test (`test_tool_result_conforms_to_output_schema`) with a
  `DSMSummary` / `DSMTooLargePayload` case so the new union members validate against `outputSchema`.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest -q` (full suite green; new tests included).
- `uv run ruff check` + `uv run ruff format --check` (CI parity).
- Live wire check: drive `archy mcp` over stdio (as in the #228 smoke) — confirm `archy_dsm(path)` and
  `archy_graph(path)` return the compact summaries, `response_format="full"` returns the heavy
  payloads, an oversized full DSM returns `DSMTooLargePayload`, and every branch's `structuredContent`
  still validates against the tool's `outputSchema`.
- Measure before/after `structuredContent` bytes on archy itself to confirm the token reduction.
- DeepWork review (incl. doc-sync + archy-grounded structural + adversarial) clean before PR.

## Release / sequencing note
Touches `src/archy/` behavior (new param + default change) → a user-visible feature change. Per the
repo's release rule this warrants a release, batched-by-theme with the rest of the MCP sweep; no
plugin-pin bump (still 19 tools). Decision deferred to the user at merge time. Next in tracker #230
after this: #229 (error-model standardization), then #227 (consolidation epic).

Good question — that's exactly the #227 consolidation epic, and it's worth settling now because **#226's design either sets it up cleanly or fights it.** Here's the concrete surface-reduction map I'd propose (19 → 13), grouped by the redundancy clusters the tracker (#230) flagged:

## How to get 19 → 13 (via mode/lens params, no capability lost)

| Cluster | Today | Consolidated | Mechanism | Saves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Graph** | `archy_graph`, `archy_graph_summary`, `archy_graph_focus` | **`archy_graph`** (one tool) | `response_format=summary\|full` (the #226 work) + `focus=`/`depth=`/`direction=` for the neighborhood mode | −2 |
| **Refactor** | `archy_hotspots`, `archy_high_risk_modules`, `archy_what_to_refactor_next` | **`archy_what_to_refactor_next`** | `lens=behavioral\|structural\|fused` (it already fuses the other two; they become lens slices) | −2 |
| **Impact** | `archy_impact`, `archy_affected` | **`archy_impact`** | `mode=blast\|affected` (affected = depth-capped + test-classified) | −1 |
| **Score** | `archy_score`, `archy_record_baseline` | **`archy_score`** | drop the wrapper; agents call `score(record=True)` | −1 |

The other 9 (`cycles`, `check`, `contracts`, `trend`, `snapshot`, `diff`, `simulate`, `dsm`, `status`) are distinct verbs/representations — folding them would hurt clarity more than it helps. `archy_dsm` stays separate from the graph cluster because it's a genuinely different output shape (positional matrix), not a view of the same dump.

That lands at **13 tools** (~30% fewer descriptions in context, which is the actual win — tool defs are always-loaded tokens and large counts degrade selection accuracy).

## Why it's a separate ticket, not part of #226

Consolidation **removes/renames tools = a breaking change** for anything pinned to the current names. The tracker deliberately sequences it **last**, at a version boundary, because it needs: a plugin-pin lower-bound bump, tool-count updates across every manifest/README/doc, and a deliberate major-ish version. #226 by contrast adds an optional param and changes a default — **no tool removed**, so it ships cleanly with no pin churn.

## The key point: #226 already paves the runway

My #226 plan makes `archy_graph(response_format="summary")` return **the exact same `GraphSummaryPayload` shape** that `archy_graph_summary` returns today. So when #227 deletes `archy_graph_summary`, callers just move to `archy_graph(response_format="summary")` with zero shape change. Same idea for `what_to_refactor_next` already being the fused superset. **#226 makes #227 a near-mechanical removal rather than a redesign.**

# Plan: #226 — concise-by-default responses on `archy_dsm` / `archy_graph`

## Context

archy exposes 19 read-only MCP tools. A few return large payloads straight into the agent's
context with no compact-by-default mode and no cap:
- `archy_dsm` returns the full sparse matrix (every cell + every module name in `ordering`/`groups`);
  ~13KB on archy itself, ~57KB on larger repos (flagged earlier as the bounded-output antipattern).
- `archy_graph` dumps up to `max_nodes=500` nodes with all node/edge attrs (~42KB measured).

Best practice (Anthropic *writing-tools-for-agents*; the 2025-06-18 sweep, tracker #230) is
**concise-by-default with a `response_format` enum** so the agent opts into the heavy payload, plus
a cap with explicit truncation indicators. This is the first behavior-changing ticket of the sweep
(#225 annotations and #228 structured-output were metadata/contract only) and has the highest
agent-edit-loop impact.

**Decision taken (user):** default `response_format="summary"` for **both** tools. No-arg calls
return concise output; `response_format="full"` returns the heavy payload (capped).

## Design

### New param (both tools)
Add `response_format: str = "summary"` to `archy_dsm` and `archy_graph`. Validate
`in {"summary", "full"}`, else raise `ValueError(f"response_format must be 'summary' or 'full'; got {response_format!r}")`
— matches the existing validation convention in `mcp.py` (e.g. `_run_graph_focus` direction check).

### `archy_graph`
- `summary` (default): delegate to the existing `_run_graph_summary` path (returns the proven
  `GraphSummaryPayload`: top-N fan-in/out/PageRank/edit-risk + external deps). Reuse `top_n` (default 20).
- `full`: existing `_run_graph_dump` (→ `GraphPayload | GraphTooLargePayload`, `max_nodes` guard unchanged).
- Return union becomes `GraphSummaryPayload | GraphPayload | GraphTooLargePayload`.
- Keep the separate `archy_graph_summary` tool for now (removing it is tool-removal = the #227
  consolidation epic). Note the equivalence in both tools' descriptions.

### `archy_dsm`
- New compact model `DSMSummary` in `src/archy/dsm.py` (frozen `BaseModel`), bounded independent of
  module count (the full DSM's size is dominated by `ordering`/`groups.members` + `cells`):
  - `group_by`, `weight` (echo)
  - `module_count` (= len ordering), `cell_count` (= len cells), `group_count`
  - `groups: tuple[DSMGroupSummary, ...]` where `DSMGroupSummary = {label, size}` — block structure
    WITHOUT the member name lists
  - `back_edge_count` + `top_back_edges: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]` (a few source→target names that
    sit above the diagonal in the ordering = the cycle-localizing signal; cap ~10). Reuse the
    back-edge convention already used by `diff_dsm`'s `new_back_edges` (cell with `row < col` after
    topological/SCC ordering).
  - `cross_group_edge_count` (edges whose endpoints fall in different groups = coupling)
  - Add a `summarize_dsm(dsm: DSM) -> DSMSummary` pure helper in `dsm.py` (derives all fields from an
    already-built `DSM`, so `build_dsm` stays unchanged and the CLI is unaffected).
- `summary` (default): `summarize_dsm(build_dsm(...))`.
- `full`: existing `build_dsm(...)` → `DSM`, but capped (see below).
- Diff path (`baseline_path` set) is unchanged — `DSMDiff` is already compact (`new_back_edges` is the
  signal) and is a deliberate diff, not a dump. `response_format` does not apply to the diff path
  (document this).
- Return union becomes `DSMSummary | DSM | DSMDiff | DSMTooLargePayload | DSMErrorPayload`.

### Truncation cap (full mode only)
Mirror the existing `GraphTooLargePayload` union-refusal pattern (consistent, deterministic, no
token-counting). For `archy_dsm(response_format="full")`, if `len(cells) > max_cells` (new
`DEFAULT_MAX_DSM_CELLS`, ~2000), return a new `DSMTooLargePayload`
`{error, cell_count, max_cells}` whose message points to `response_format="summary"` /
`focus=` / `package=` as the escape hatches (same shape/wording style as `GraphTooLargePayload`).
`archy_graph` full mode keeps its existing `max_nodes`→`GraphTooLargePayload` guard.

### Out of scope (deliberate)
- CLI (`archy dsm`, `archy graph`) stays unchanged — confirmed independent of the MCP code paths;
  renders to a human-driven terminal; this ticket is MCP-scoped.
- Removing/folding `archy_graph_summary` → #227 (BC-breaking, sequenced last).
- Tool count stays 19 → no plugin-pin bump, no manifest/registry count edits.

## Files to change

### Code
- `src/archy/dsm.py` — add `DSMGroupSummary`, `DSMSummary` models + `summarize_dsm()` helper.
- `src/archy/mcp.py` —
  - import `DSMSummary` (+ `summarize_dsm`); add `DSMTooLargePayload` model + `DEFAULT_MAX_DSM_CELLS`.
  - `archy_dsm`: new `response_format` param, branch summary/full, cap full mode, widen return union +
    rewrite `description=`.
  - `archy_graph`: new `response_format` param, branch summary(→`_run_graph_summary`)/full, widen
    return union + rewrite `description=`; surface `top_n`.
  - `archy_graph_summary` description: cross-reference `archy_graph(response_format="summary")`.
  - `_AGENT_LOOP_PROMPT`: update the `archy_dsm` / graph guidance to reflect summary-by-default.

### Docs (thorough — the user's explicit ask; the doc-sync `.deepreview` rule also enforces drift)
- `README.md` — MCP tool table rows for `archy_dsm`, `archy_graph`, `archy_graph_summary`
  (~lines 257–263): document `response_format`, the summary default, and the cap. Touch the
  "Tool output contract" note (~line 270) only if needed.
- `docs/SPEC_GRAPH_MCP.md` — the design source of truth for the three graph tools: add
  `response_format` + summary-default + cap to the `archy_graph` section (and note the

- `docs/AGENT_LOOP.md` — update the `archy_graph` / `archy_dsm` call examples for summary-by-default.
- `plugins/claude/skills/archy/SKILL.md` — update any dsm/graph call examples to match (it mirrors

  entries — do not rewrite; add a new dated entry only if the file's pattern calls for one.

def diff_dsm(before: DSM, after: DSM) -> DSMDiff:
    """Diff two DSMs by (source_name, target_name).

    Operates on names rather than positions so the diff is meaningful
    when reordering changes (e.g. after community detection re-runs on
    a slightly different graph). `new_back_edges` is computed in
    `after`'s ordering: an edge is a back-edge if the source is later in
    `after.ordering` than the target.
    """
    before_edges = _name_indexed(before)
    after_edges = _name_indexed(after)
    after_pos = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(after.ordering)}

    added: list[DSMCell] = []
    removed: list[DSMCell] = []
    weight_changed: list[tuple[DSMCell, DSMCell]] = []
    new_back_edges: list[DSMCell] = []

    for key, after_cell in after_edges.items():
        if key not in before_edges:
            added.append(after_cell)
            row_name, col_name = key
            if (
                row_name in after_pos
                and col_name in after_pos
                and after_pos[row_name] > after_pos[col_name]
            ):
                new_back_edges.append(after_cell)
        else:
            before_cell = before_edges[key]
            if before_cell.weight != after_cell.weight:
                weight_changed.append((before_cell, after_cell))

    for key, before_cell in before_edges.items():
        if key not in after_edges:
            removed.append(before_cell)

    before_nodes = set(before.ordering)
    after_nodes = set(after.ordering)
    nodes_added = tuple(sorted(after_nodes - before_nodes))
    nodes_removed = tuple(sorted(before_nodes - after_nodes))

    added.sort(key=lambda c: (c.row, c.col))
    removed.sort(key=lambda c: (c.row, c.col))
    new_back_edges.sort(key=lambda c: (c.row, c.col))

    return DSMDiff(
        added=tuple(added),
        removed=tuple(removed),
        weight_changed=tuple(weight_changed),

"""Design Structure Matrix (DSM): builder, renderers, and diff.

A DSM is the canonical industrial view of system coupling (Steward 1981,
Eppinger & Browning, MacCormack 2006): nodes go on both axes in a chosen
order, and the cell at (row=source, col=target) is non-empty when the
source depends on the target. Reading positionally exposes properties
that any single scalar would hide: back-edges sit above the diagonal in
topological orderings, community structure becomes block-diagonal under
community grouping, and layer violations are off-block entries under
layer grouping.

archy ships DSM as a visualization-only output (no axis, no diagnostic
scalar) per `docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md`. The intended consumer is an LLM
coding agent that reads the matrix as structured context, not a human
browsing a dashboard.
"""

class DSMGroupSummary(BaseModel):
    """A group's label and size, without its member name list.

    The full `DSMGroup.members` tuples are the bulk of a large DSM's payload
    (every module name, repeated in `ordering`); the summary keeps only the
    block structure (how many blocks, how big) that orients an agent.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    label: str
    size: int


class DSMSummary(BaseModel):
    """Compact, count-oriented view of a DSM for concise-by-default output.

    Derived from an already-built `DSM` by `summarize_dsm`; carries the
    block structure and the cycle-localizing back-edges without the full
    `cells`/`ordering`/`members`, so its size is bounded by the number of
    groups (plus a capped back-edge sample) rather than the module count.
    An agent that needs the full matrix re-requests with
    `response_format="full"`.

    `back_edges` are the load-bearing signal: cells whose source sits later
    in `ordering` than the target (`row > col`), i.e. an edge that points
    against the chosen order -- the same back-edge test `diff_dsm` uses for
    `new_back_edges`. `cross_group_edge_count` is the inter-block coupling
    (edges whose endpoints fall in different groups).
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    group_by: GroupBy
    weight: Weight
    module_count: int
    cell_count: int
    group_count: int
    groups: tuple[DSMGroupSummary, ...]
    back_edge_count: int
    back_edges: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]
    cross_group_edge_count: int


# Cap on the back-edge sample surfaced in a DSMSummary. Back-edge *count* is
# always exact; this only bounds the (source, target) name pairs listed, since
# a deeply tangled graph could otherwise reintroduce an unbounded payload.
SUMMARY_BACK_EDGE_SAMPLE = 10


def summarize_dsm(dsm: DSM) -> DSMSummary:
    """Project a built `DSM` into its compact `DSMSummary` (no full cells).

    Pure function of the DSM: `build_dsm` and the CLI are untouched. Group
    membership is read positionally from `ordering` (groups are contiguous
    slices), so a cell crosses groups when its row and col fall in different
    blocks.
    """
    group_of: dict[int, int] = {}
    offset = 0
    for gi, g in enumerate(dsm.groups):
        for pos in range(offset, offset + len(g.members)):
            group_of[pos] = gi
        offset += len(g.members)

    back_edges = [c for c in dsm.cells if c.row > c.col]
    cross_group = sum(
        1 for c in dsm.cells if group_of.get(c.row) != group_of.get(c.col)
    )

    return DSMSummary(
        group_by=dsm.group_by,
        weight=dsm.weight,
        module_count=len(dsm.ordering),
        cell_count=len(dsm.cells),
        group_count=len(dsm.groups),
        groups=tuple(DSMGroupSummary(label=g.label, size=len(g.members)) for g in dsm.groups),
        back_edge_count=len(back_edges),
        back_edges=tuple(
            (dsm.ordering[c.row], dsm.ordering[c.col])
            for c in back_edges[:SUMMARY_BACK_EDGE_SAMPLE]
        ),
        cross_group_edge_count=cross_group,
    )

def summarize_dsm(dsm: DSM) -> DSMSummary:
    """Project a built `DSM` into its compact `DSMSummary` (no full cells).

    Pure function of the DSM: `build_dsm` and the CLI are untouched. Group
    membership is read positionally from `ordering` (groups are contiguous
    slices), so a cell crosses groups when its row and col fall in different
    blocks.
    """
    group_of: dict[int, int] = {}
    offset = 0
    for gi, g in enumerate(dsm.groups):
        for pos in range(offset, offset + len(g.members)):
            group_of[pos] = gi
        offset += len(g.members)

        1 for c in dsm.cells if group_of.get(c.row) != group_of.get(c.col)
    )

        group_by=dsm.group_by,
        weight=dsm.weight,
        module_count=len(dsm.ordering),
        cell_count=len(dsm.cells),
        group_count=len(dsm.groups),
        groups=tuple(DSMGroupSummary(label=g.label, size=len(g.members)) for g in dsm.groups),
        back_edge_count=len(back_edges),
        back_edges=tuple(
            (dsm.ordering[c.row], dsm.ordering[c.col])
            for c in back_edges[:SUMMARY_BACK_EDGE_SAMPLE]
        ),
        cross_group_edge_count=cross_group,

def test_all_tools_declare_output_schema():
    # 2025-06-18 structured output: FastMCP derives an `outputSchema` (JSON
    # Schema) from each tool's return annotation. Assert every tool declares
    # one and it is an object schema, since `structuredContent` must be a JSON
    # object (sequence/union returns are wrapped under a `result` key to honor
    # this -- see the module docstring).
    server = create_server()
    tools = asyncio.run(server.list_tools())
    for tool in tools:
        schema = tool.outputSchema
        assert schema is not None, f"{tool.name} has no outputSchema"
        assert schema.get("type") == "object", f"{tool.name} outputSchema is not an object"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    # One case per wrapping rule the structured-output contract has to honor.
    # expect_text is the BC guidance that a `TextContent` block accompanies
    # `structuredContent`; it is False only for an empty bare-sequence return,
    # which FastMCP serializes to zero content blocks (the documented benign
    # edge in the module docstring).
    ("name", "extra_args", "expect_text"),
    [
        ("archy_score", {}, True),  # BaseModel return
        ("archy_graph", {}, True),  # union, success branch (GraphPayload)
        ("archy_diff", {}, True),  # union, in-band error branch (no baseline -> DiffErrorPayload)
        ("archy_cycles", {}, False),  # bare list, empty on an acyclic project -> {"result": []}
    ],
)
def test_tool_result_conforms_to_output_schema(
    acyclic_project: Path, name: str, extra_args: dict, expect_text: bool
):
    # A client that validates `structuredContent` against a declared
    # `outputSchema` MUST NOT reject archy's results -- including the in-band
    # `*ErrorPayload` branch of a union return, which is an `anyOf` member of
    # the schema, not a separate error channel.
    from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator

    server = create_server()
    schema = {t.name: t.outputSchema for t in asyncio.run(server.list_tools())}[name]
    content, structured = asyncio.run(
        server.call_tool(name, {"path": str(acyclic_project), **extra_args})
    )
    assert isinstance(structured, dict)
    errors = sorted(
        Draft202012Validator(schema).iter_errors(structured), key=lambda e: list(e.path)
    )
    assert not errors, f"{name} structuredContent violates outputSchema: {errors[:1]}"
    has_text = any(getattr(block, "text", None) for block in content)
    assert has_text is expect_text

def _dsm(path: Path, response_format: str = "summary", **kw):
    base = dict(
        group_by="community",
        weight="imports",
        focus=None,
        focus_depth=1,
        package=None,
        baseline_path=None,
    )
    base.update(kw)
    return _run_dsm(path, response_format=response_format, **base)

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import networkx as nx
import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError

from archy.dsm import (
    DSM,
    DSMCell,
    DSMGroup,
    build_dsm,
    diff_dsm,
    dsm_from_dict,
    read_dsm,
    render_ascii,
    render_diff_text,
    render_json,
    write_dsm,
)


def _g(*edges: tuple[str, str], calls: dict[tuple[str, str], int] | None = None) -> nx.DiGraph:
    g: nx.DiGraph = nx.DiGraph()
    for u, v in edges:
        cc = (calls or {}).get((u, v), 0)
        g.add_edge(u, v, lines=(1,), call_count=cc)
    return g


def _externalize(g: nx.DiGraph, *names: str) -> nx.DiGraph:
    for n in names:
        g.add_node(n, external=True)
    return g


# --- Builder: basic shapes ----------------------------------------------------


def test_build_dsm_empty_graph():
    dsm = build_dsm(nx.DiGraph())
    assert dsm.ordering == ()
    assert dsm.cells == ()
    assert dsm.groups == ()


def test_build_dsm_single_node():
    g = nx.DiGraph()
    g.add_node("a")
    dsm = build_dsm(g)
    assert dsm.ordering == ("a",)
    assert dsm.cells == ()
    assert len(dsm.groups) == 1


def test_build_dsm_excludes_external_nodes():
    g = _g(("a", "b"))
    _externalize(g, "stdlib_thing")
    g.add_edge("a", "stdlib_thing")

257	| `archy_graph_focus` | Bounded subgraph around one or more modules (qualnames or file paths). `depth` caps hops; `direction` is `in`/`out`/`both`. Each edge carries import line numbers. Use before editing for a richer view than `archy_impact`. |
258	| `archy_graph_summary` | Top-N modules by fan-in, fan-out, and PageRank, plus top external dependencies. Whole-project overview sized for LLM context. |
259	| `archy_graph` | Full dependency-graph dump matching `archy graph --format json`. Refuses graphs larger than `max_nodes` (default 500) to avoid blowing context; bump the limit explicitly when you really want everything. |
260	| `archy_high_risk_modules` | Top-N internal modules by `edit_risk`: geometric mean of propagation cost, normalized fan-in, and Martin's instability. Each entry breaks the composite back out. Call before a non-trivial edit to decide whether to scope down or pause for review. |
261	| `archy_hotspots` | Rank internal modules by `cc_sum x git-commit-count` (Tornhill / CodeScene's "Code Red"). Each entry is `{module, path, cc_sum, churn, score}`; zero-CC and zero-churn rows are filtered. `since` is passed straight to `git log --since`. Answers "where is the refactoring leverage?"; the structural cousin `archy_high_risk_modules` answers "is this edit dangerous?" without needing git. If the project isn't under git, returns an empty list plus a `note` so the agent can pivot. |
262	| `archy_what_to_refactor_next` | One ranked refactor-priority list fusing both lenses, so you call once instead of `archy_hotspots` + `archy_high_risk_modules` + your own synthesis. Sums the behavioral lens (CC x churn) and the structural lens (edit-risk: central+fragile) into a `priority`, so a module flagged by *both* generally outranks a comparable single-lens one (a dominant single-lens signal can still rank first); each entry names which lenses fired and carries a one-line `rationale`. `min_risk` is the structural floor. Without git, the ranking is structural-only. An empty list plus a `note` is a real answer: nothing is both complex+churned and nothing is central+fragile above the floor. |
263	| `archy_dsm` | Design Structure Matrix view of the import graph. `group_by` controls row/col ordering (`community` for block-diagonal cohesion, `layer` for layer-violation forensics, `topological` to localize back-edges). `weight` is `imports` or `calls`. Narrow large projects with `focus=<qualname>` + `focus_depth` or `package=<prefix>`. When `baseline_path` is provided, returns a structured diff whose `new_back_edges` field flags cycles the edit just introduced. Visualization-only; see [`docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md`](docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md). |
264	| `archy_status` | Report the persistent index's freshness: `last_synced_at`, `cached_files`, and whether the background watcher is `watching`. The `archy mcp` server keeps a debounced filesystem watcher warming `.archy/index.db` so graph builds stay fast; every tool also syncs on demand, so results are never stale even when `last_synced_at` looks a moment behind. |
265

# Spec: `archy_graph` MCP tool

Open roadmap item from README:

> `archy graph` MCP tool: expose the dep graph itself for agent-side reasoning

The CLI command `archy graph` already exists and emits `text` / `json` / `dot`. The work is wiring it into `src/archy/mcp.py` next to the other nine tools - but a naïve "dump the full graph JSON" tool wastes the agent's context on every call. This spec defines a small set of lenses tuned for how agents actually reason about a graph.

## Why not one big dump

A full graph for a medium project (a few hundred modules, a few thousand edges) easily blows past 100k tokens once you include node attrs (`path`, `is_package`, `external`, `instability`) and edge attrs (`lines`, `is_relative`). Agents rarely need all of it - they need:

- "what does this module depend on / who depends on it"  (the local neighborhood - the by-far most common query)
- "what's the shape of the whole project"  (a summary view, not 3000 edges)
- "give me everything so I can do my own analysis"  (rare, but the CLI already serves this)

The other dep-graph MCP servers we surveyed converge on the same split:

- **sentrux** ships a `dsm` (Dependency Structure Matrix) tool - a compact whole-graph summary, distinct from the raw-graph endpoint
- **mkearl/dependency-mcp** has `get_dependency_graph` (full) *and* `get_file_metadata` (single-file focus)
- **entrepeneur4lyf/code-graph-mcp** exposes `find_callers` / `find_callees` - neighborhood queries, not full dumps
- **oraios/serena** is the strongest signal here: "agent-first tool design… robust high-level abstractions… distinguishing it from approaches that rely on low-level concepts"

Takeaway: a `graph` namespace with three tools, not one.

## Proposed tools

### 1. `archy_graph_focus(path, modules, depth=1, direction="both")`

The primary tool. Returns a slice of the graph centered on one or more modules.

**Parameters**
- `modules: list[str]` - qualnames (e.g. `["archy.parser"]`) **or** file paths that resolve to internal modules (uses the shared `resolve_modules` helper, same path resolution as `find_impact`). Multi-seed: ego graphs are unioned across all resolved seeds; unresolved entries are returned in the `unresolved` field instead of erroring.
- `depth: int = 1` - how many hops to expand
- `direction: "in" | "out" | "both" = "both"` - `in` = who depends on me (callers), `out` = my dependencies, `both` = bidirectional neighborhood
- `internal_only: bool = True`

**Returns** - same `_graph_to_dict` shape the CLI emits, but only the subgraph reachable within `depth` hops in the requested direction(s). Each node carries `instability`; each edge carries `lines` so the agent can pinpoint the import site.

**Why this shape**: `find_impact` already gives reverse-reachability of *internal* modules; this generalizes it (forward direction, depth-limited, with edge detail). Agents use this before editing - same role as `archy_impact` but more flexible.

### 2. `archy_graph_summary(path, top_n=20)`

The whole-project lens, sized for context.

**Returns**
```
{
  "module_count": int,
  "internal_edge_count": int,
  "external_edge_count": int,
  "parse_errors": [qualname, ...],
  "top_fan_in":  [{module, in_degree, instability}, ...],   # top_n
  "top_fan_out": [{module, out_degree, instability}, ...],  # top_n
  "top_pagerank": [{module, score}, ...],                   # top_n

Fan-in/fan-out + instability is the cheapest possible "where is the gravity in this codebase" answer. This is what `dsm` is in sentrux, minus the full matrix (which doesn't paginate well into LLM context).

### 3. `archy_graph(path, internal_only=True, max_nodes=500)`

The escape hatch. Full graph dump, matching `archy graph --format json` exactly, with a guardrail.

- If `node_count > max_nodes`, return an error payload pointing the agent at `archy_graph_focus` / `archy_graph_summary` instead of silently truncating. Truncated graphs lie (missing edges look like absence of dependency).
- `max_nodes` is overridable so a determined caller can opt in.

## Response models

Add to `src/archy/mcp.py`:

```python
class GraphNode(BaseModel):
    id: str
    external: bool
    path: str | None = None          # internal only
    is_package: bool | None = None   # internal only
    instability: float | None = None # internal only

class GraphEdge(BaseModel):
    source: str
    target: str
    is_relative: bool
    lines: tuple[int, ...]

class GraphPayload(BaseModel):
    root: str | None
    parse_errors: tuple[str, ...]
    nodes: tuple[GraphNode, ...]
    edges: tuple[GraphEdge, ...]
    unresolved: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # from focus(): refs that matched no internal module

# Separate model rather than a `truncated: bool` flag so the typed union
# (`GraphPayload | GraphTooLargePayload`) forces callers to handle the
# refusal case explicitly instead of silently treating a truncated graph
# as complete.
class GraphTooLargePayload(BaseModel):
    error: str
    node_count: int
    max_nodes: int

class GraphSummaryEntry(BaseModel):
    module: str
    value: float                     # in_degree | out_degree | pagerank | importer_count
    instability: float | None = None

class GraphSummaryPayload(BaseModel):
    module_count: int
    internal_edge_count: int
    external_edge_count: int
    parse_errors: tuple[str, ...]
    top_fan_in: tuple[GraphSummaryEntry, ...]
    top_fan_out: tuple[GraphSummaryEntry, ...]
    top_pagerank: tuple[GraphSummaryEntry, ...]
    external_deps: tuple[GraphSummaryEntry, ...]
```

## Implementation notes

- **PageRank** - hand-rolled power iteration (~15 lines) in `mcp.py::_pagerank`. NetworkX 3.x's `pagerank` requires numpy/scipy, which archy keeps out of the runtime install. A `parity` dependency group + `pytest.importorskip("numpy")` test gates the comparison against `nx.pagerank` so we can validate correctness locally without making numpy a hard dep.
- **Module resolution for `focus`** - extract the `find_impact` file-to-qualname helper into a shared util; the focus tool needs the same logic.
- **Subgraph extraction** - `nx.ego_graph(g, module, radius=depth, undirected=False)` for `out`; reverse the graph for `in`; union the two for `both`. Don't roll your own BFS.
- **Touch tests for parity** - every shape returned by `archy_graph` must round-trip against `_graph_to_dict` output for a fixture project; this is the contract that lets agents and the CLI agree.

## Update prompt + agent loop

Add a one-liner to the `loop` MCP prompt: before editing a module, prefer `archy_graph_focus(module=…, depth=1)` over `archy_impact` when you want *both* directions or want to see edge line numbers. `archy_impact` stays as the dedicated blast-radius tool (it answers a slightly different question: transitive reverse-reachability of internal modules only, which `focus` could match with `direction="in", depth=∞` but that's not the agent's mental model).

## Out of scope (intentionally)

- **Call graph edges** - already a separate roadmap item in `FUTURE.md` line 17. When that lands, all three tools get the new edge type for free if we plumb a `kind` attr through. Don't pre-empt the design here.
- **Persistent caching** - the dependency-mcp prior art has a 1h TTL cache; archy graphs build fast enough on every call that this is premature.
- **DOT format over MCP** - the CLI keeps DOT for humans piping to graphviz; MCP clients want JSON.

1. Extract `_graph_to_dict` into shared module; CLI + MCP both call it.
2. Add the three tools with response models and tests.
3. Update README: tick the `archy graph` MCP roadmap box; add the three tool names to the tool list near `archy mcp`.

3:Short, opinionated summary of where archy is going. The detailed item-by-item list (with shipped, in-flight, deferred, and rejected items, plus citations to the literature each idea came from) lives in [`FUTURE.md`](FUTURE.md). This page is the executive summary.
5:## Audience principle (load-bearing)
14:## Now
16:Things actively in flight or planned for the next 2-3 releases. Items previously in this section shipped in v0.21.0 / v0.22.0 / v0.24.0 / v0.25.0; the queue below promotes from "Next" as work picks up.
18:Both phases of [`SPEC_INDEX_AND_INSTALL.md`](SPEC_INDEX_AND_INSTALL.md) have shipped (Phase 1 install-DX in v0.25.0/v0.26.0, Phase 2 persistent index + watcher in v0.27.0); see "Shipped from this section" below. The remaining queued items are in "Next".
20:### Shipped from this section
22:- ~~Phase 2: persistent index + file watcher~~ shipped in v0.27.0 ([#116](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/pull/116) cache, [#118](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/pull/118) watcher + `archy_status`). Part 1: `src/archy/index.py` caches each file's `ParseResult` in `.archy/index.db` keyed by content hash and re-parses only what changed, then re-runs the existing global resolution, so a cache-backed build is byte-identical to a cold one (the property the test suite asserts). Benchmarked 7-9x warm-path speedups on Django (2.9k modules), pytorch (4.5k), and Home Assistant (17.3k); parsing is ~85% of cold build cost and resolution stays ~3%, which is why the cache boundary is the parse, not the resolved graph, and why incremental resolution was rejected. Part 2: `src/archy/watcher.py`'s `IndexManager` holds one persistent cache connection per project root and a `watchdog` observer that runs the sync in the background on a 2-second debounce (`threading.Timer` reset per Python-file event), all serialized by one lock; the `archy mcp` server keeps a per-root manager registry so repeated tool calls reuse a warm, background-synced index. A new `archy_status` MCP tool (the 17th) reports `last_synced_at`, `cached_files`, and whether the watcher is running. The watcher is a latency optimization, never a correctness mechanism: every tool still syncs on demand, so a result is never stale even if an event was missed or the watcher could not start. Remaining optional follow-up: the churn column (git-log-populated, surfaced in `archy_hotspots`).
24:- ~~Agent-detecting installer registry (`archy install` / `archy uninstall`)~~ shipped in v0.26.0 ([#112](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/pull/112) install, [#113](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/pull/113) uninstall + docs). Phase 1 (third leg) of [`SPEC_INDEX_AND_INSTALL.md`](SPEC_INDEX_AND_INSTALL.md), closing the install-DX leg. `archy install` auto-detects which agent clients (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Continue) are present, writes each one's MCP server stanza, drops the rules file each expects (`.cursor/rules/archy.mdc`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, ...), and for Claude Code seeds the `permissions.allow` allowlist the plugin manifest cannot write (closing the #104 gap). Architecturally an "adapter registry": one small adapter per client in `src/archy/install/adapters/`, cross-platform from day one (detection layers `shutil.which` over per-OS config-path probes with macOS-app-bundle / Windows-install-dir fallbacks). `archy uninstall` is the symmetric inverse: each adapter declares paired `render`/`unrender` per file, so uninstall strips archy from shared configs (leaving the rest byte-for-byte) and deletes archy-owned files; idempotent. Non-interactive flags (`--yes`, `--target`, `--print-config`, `--dry-run`) for CI / scripting. Five-layer test strategy (unit, snapshot, filesystem integration, contract, gated E2E) per [`SPEC_INSTALL_TESTING.md`](SPEC_INSTALL_TESTING.md), running on the ubuntu/macos/windows matrix. User-facing docs: [`INSTALL.md`](INSTALL.md).
25:- ~~`archy affected` CLI + `archy_affected` MCP tool~~ shipped in v0.25.0 ([#103](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/pull/103)). Phase 1 (first leg) of [`SPEC_INDEX_AND_INSTALL.md`](SPEC_INDEX_AND_INSTALL.md). Maps changed files to impacted modules and test files via a depth-capped reverse-impact walk (default 5 hops) so monorepo edits stay tractable, with the impacted set pre-classified into `impacted_tests` (pytest convention by default, recursive-glob override via `--filter`) and `impacted_modules`. CLI shape is `git diff --name-only HEAD | archy affected . --stdin -q | xargs pytest`; MCP shape mirrors the same payload. Internal modules only at launch; `--include-external` follow-up captured in [`FUTURE.md`](FUTURE.md). Inspired by [colbymchenry/codegraph](https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph)'s `affected` command, scoped to archy's judge-not-librarian role (see [`LEARNINGS.md`](LEARNINGS.md) bucket 6).
26:- ~~Claude Code plugin~~ shipped in v0.25.0 ([#104](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/pull/104)). Phase 1 (second leg) of the install-DX work. Bundles the MCP server registration (`uvx archy>=0.25 mcp`) and the canonical `archy` skill into an installable unit at `plugins/claude/`; users run `claude --plugin-dir /path/to/archy/plugins/claude` to install. Two limitations of the current Claude Code plugin loader documented inline: plugin manifests cannot seed `permissions.allow` (paste-into-`settings.json` snippet shipped in the README instead) and cannot bundle a project-level `CLAUDE.md` (instruction context flows through the bundled skill). Drift between the canonical `skills/archy/SKILL.md` and the plugin's mirror is pinned by `tests/test_plugin.py`.
27:- ~~Smarter `archy_diff` summary~~ shipped in v0.24.0. `archy diff` / `archy_diff` returns an additive `DiffSummary` block (`headline`, `top_regressions`, `top_improvements`) ranked by `compute_edit_risk` so the loop-closer step doesn't have to scan and re-rank raw deltas. Detail lists stay; ranking is additive so existing consumers don't break. Cycle descriptions truncate to 5 members + `(+N more)` to keep dagster-sized SCCs readable. Empirical perf on the 28-repo dogfood: `summarize_diff` is 0.1-0.5% of total `archy diff` runtime even on the largest real repos, so shipped additive with no opt-out. MCP `loop` prompt and `AGENT_LOOP.md` updated to direct agents to read `summary.headline` first.
28:- ~~`archy dsm` (Design Structure Matrix)~~ shipped in v0.22.0 as a visualization-only output. CLI `archy dsm PATH` + MCP tool `archy_dsm`, with `--group=community|layer|topological`, `--weight=imports|calls`, `--focus`/`--package` filters, and `--diff` returning a `DSMDiff` whose `new_back_edges` field flags cycles an edit just introduced. ASCII for terminal context, JSON for tool consumption; HTML output dropped per the audience principle. Empirical study against the 27-project bench ruled out promoting any DSM-derived scalar to a score axis or diagnostic ([`DSM_EMPIRICS.md`](research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md)).
29:- ~~Call-weighted Newman Q as a refinement of the modularity axis~~ shipped in v0.21.0 as a parallel diagnostic on `archy score` rather than an axis replacement. The gap between unweighted and weighted Q is the load-bearing signal (it detects mismatch between import-graph and call-graph community structure). Replacement was rejected because directionality is contested for intentional small-core / broad-call shapes ([`CALL_WEIGHTED_Q_EMPIRICS.md`](research/CALL_WEIGHTED_Q_EMPIRICS.md)).
30:- ~~`archy_what_to_refactor_next` MCP tool~~ shipped in v0.30.0 ([#130](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/130)). One ranked refactor-priority list (CLI `archy what-to-refactor-next` + MCP `archy_what_to_refactor_next`, the 19th tool) fusing the behavioral lens (`archy_hotspots`, CC x churn) and the structural lens (`archy_high_risk_modules`, edit-risk): candidates come from both, and the fused `priority` (each lens normalized to its project max, then summed) ranks a module flagged by *both* lenses above a comparable single-lens one, while still letting a dominant single-lens signal (a giant hotspot at the import-graph leaves) top the list. Each entry names which lenses fired plus a one-line `rationale`. Pure aggregation over the two existing primitives in `src/archy/refactor.py`; no new analysis. Honest null is load-bearing: the candidate set is empty (and the tool returns a `note`, not a phantom #1) when nothing is both complex and churned and nothing clears the `min_risk` structural floor (default 0.15) - a real "nothing to prioritize" answer for small, young, or clean projects. Git-absent degrades to the structural lens alone, mirroring `archy_hotspots`.
32:## Next
42:## Deferred (needs more thought)
45:- **Equality based on per-function CC.** Currently a proxy via Gini over module out-degrees. The eventual signal is `gini(per_function_cyclomatic_complexity)`; requires the cyclomatic-complexity metric (shipped in v0.17, promoted to a score axis as `complexity` in v0.20), but the substitution itself has not been validated yet.
49:## Rejected (explicitly will not ship)
52:- **`calls_per_edge` as a 6th score axis.** Empirical study in 2026-05 ([`AXIS_REVIEW.md`](research/AXIS_REVIEW.md)) concluded against axis promotion on directionality / actionability / discriminant-validity grounds even though independence passes. The call data is genuinely useful and shipped as: a diagnostic on `archy score`, the v0.21 call-weighted Newman Q parallel diagnostic, and the LocAgent-style `archy_graph_*` MCP navigation tools.
53:- **HTML output formats for archy commands.** Per the audience principle: agents consume structured JSON and terminal ASCII, not browser-rendered HTML. The original "static HTML trend report" v0.3 stretch goal and the "self-contained HTML for CI artifacts" framing of `archy dsm` are both retired. If a human dashboard is ever needed, third-party tools can consume archy's JSON output.
60:## How this list changes
62:When a "Now" item ships, it moves to a bullet in the README's "Shipped" section and gets a citation in [`FUTURE.md`](FUTURE.md) with the validation evidence. When a "Next" item gets prioritized, it moves to "Now." Items move into "Deferred" or "Rejected" only when there is empirical evidence (a benchmark sweep, an FP-rate study, a concrete user pain point) or an explicit value-prop argument (the audience principle, the structural-niche focus), not on speculation. Every shape change to this list lands as a PR so the history is in git.
64:See [`FUTURE.md`](FUTURE.md) for the long-form list with citations, [`docs/research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md`](research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md) for the literature survey that informs prioritization, [`docs/research/AXIS_REVIEW.md`](research/AXIS_REVIEW.md) for the OECD framework used on every axis-promotion decision, and [`docs/LEARNINGS.md`](LEARNINGS.md) for design rationale on shipped decisions.

5	order, and the cell at (row=source, col=target) is non-empty when the
6	source depends on the target. Reading positionally exposes properties
7	that any single scalar would hide: back-edges sit above the diagonal in
8	topological orderings, community structure becomes block-diagonal under
9	community grouping, and layer violations are off-block entries under
10	layer grouping.
11	
12	archy ships DSM as a visualization-only output (no axis, no diagnostic
13	scalar) per `docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md`. The intended consumer is an LLM
14	coding agent that reads the matrix as structured context, not a human
15	browsing a dashboard.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	from pathlib import Path
21	from typing import Literal, cast
22	
23	import networkx as nx
24	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

27	Weight = Literal["imports", "calls"]
28	
29

33	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
34

36	    col: int
37	    weight: float
38	
39

42	
43	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
44

46	    members: tuple[str, ...]

50	    """Sparse DSM. `ordering` is the row/col order; `cells` lists non-empty entries.
51	
52	    `groups[i].members` is a contiguous slice of `ordering`. Cell positions
53	    are int indices into `ordering`, so an agent can reconstruct the dense
54	    matrix by walking cells and indexing by `(row, col)`.
55	    """
56	
57	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

83	    removed: tuple[DSMCell, ...]

85	    nodes_added: tuple[str, ...]
86	    nodes_removed: tuple[str, ...]
87	    new_back_edges: tuple[DSMCell, ...]

99	
100	    label: str

with no compact mode and no cap (archy_dsm ~57KB on larger repos,

practice (Anthropic writing-tools-for-agents; MCP sweep tracker #230).
